item.stem:
[Image: A numbered axis, from 0 to 2. Two dots are shown, “P” and “Q”. “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1 and “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1.]

P and Q represent two fractions on the number line above.

P × Q = N.

Which of these shows the location of N on the number line?

options.label: A

options.label: D

item.figure_description:
The figure above the text shows a horizontal number line with an arrow at the right end. There are tick marks labeled 0, 1, and 2, with equal spacing between 0 and 1 and between 1 and 2. Between 0 and 1, two points are marked with black dots: point P is labeled below the line at approximately 0.5 (halfway between 0 and 1), and point Q is labeled below the line at approximately 0.75 (three-fourths of the distance from 0 to 1).

Each of the four response options shows the same number line with points P and Q in their original positions, along with a third point labeled N above the line:
- Option A: Point N is marked halfway between 1 and 2, at approximately 1.5.
- Option B: Point N is marked between Q and 1, at approximately 0.85.
- Option C: Point N is marked between P and Q, at approximately 0.625.
- Option D: Point N is marked between 0 and P, at approximately 0.25.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it.
